subject: Quantify AI — dedicated sizing & perf validation plan
messages:
From: Liam Chen <liam@quantify.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@quantify.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + SLO targets (Quantify / Redwood)

Diego — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying items so your team can size the dedicated pool: 

- Primary workload: real-time call transcription + short follow-on instructions. Typical response length: 40–180 tokens.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile end-to-end <= 200ms for short completions (<=64 tokens). For streaming transcripts we need token cadence such that per-token emit latency after initial chunk is <= 30ms.
- Throughput: steady-state 120 requests/sec with bursts to 200 req/sec (peak 5–10 min windows) — average tokens per req ~120.
- Concurrency goal: support ~350 concurrent inferences without QoS degradation.
- Availability/SLO: want fallbacks to cheaper model variants if reserved pool saturates.

We attached a small set of representative call recordings + expected prompt/response sizes (quantify_perf_examples.json). Next steps from our side: we can provision test keys and a short token budget for a one-day perf run.

Can your team propose a concrete validation plan (what you will measure, GPU candidates, reserved throughput targets to test) and an expected sizing recommendation (GPU count / type) to meet these SLOs?

Thanks — Liam
Liam Chen
Head of Platform
Quantify AI

Attachments: quantify_perf_examples.json
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam@quantify.ai>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@quantify.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + SLO targets (Quantify / Redwood)

Liam — great notes, thanks. Appreciate the artifact set; we reviewed the sample traces. High-level plan below and a suggested cadence for the validation run.

Plan overview (one-day dedicated validation):
1) Two-pass perf matrix against representative prompts:
   - Pass A: A100 80GB (cuda kernels tuned, fp16 / 4-bit quant where feasible)
   - Pass B: H100 80GB (nvlink config, updated attention kernels)
   - For each pass we measure: p50/p95/p99 latency (token-level + end-to-end), sustained throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache behavior for streaming sessions.
2) Reserved pool configuration to test:
   - Low-cost baseline: 6 x A100 (reserved) — optimistic throughput estimate 140 req/s for your avg tokens (estim).
   - Mid: 4 x H100 — better throughput per GPU and lower p95 in streaming cases.
   - Headroom test: add burst capacity to end-to-end pipeline to simulate 200 req/s peaks.
3) Streaming validation: run multi-client streaming sessions to verify per-token emit latency (target <= 30ms after first chunk).
4) Fallback policy test: hit the pool to saturation and validate automatic fallback to a compatible smaller-quantized model with preserved functional outputs.

Deliverables:
- Detailed perf matrix (spreadsheet) with recommended reserved capacity and buffer for 99th percentile headroom.
- A short runbook describing autoscaling / burst strategy and cost delta.
- Summary slide deck + raw traces.

We can execute the one-day run in our dedicated evaluation cluster next Thu (2027-07-29). To proceed we need: 1) approved sandbox keys, 2) a 24-hour window to run synthetic + replay traffic, 3) a short contact list for on-call during the run.

If that date works, I will schedule the run and attach the sizing matrix draft after the test.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-matrix.xlsx
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@quantify.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Liam Chen <liam@quantify.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + SLO targets (Quantify / Redwood)

Diego/Team — quick clarifications from our infra folks before the run: 

- Peak windows are typically 6–12 minutes; we can provide a trace with two representative spikes.
- We will enable detailed logging for the run but would prefer the artifacts to be kept to a 30-day retention for compliance.
- Two questions for you (please confirm):
   1) Can you run the H100 pass with nvlink enabled and report inter-GPU scatter latency?
   2) For fallback validation, can Redwood guarantee identical tokenization and deterministic post-quantized behavior for the smaller model variant?

We can provide sandbox keys today; aiming for Thu 29th is fine if you confirm the runbook and on-call list.

— Olivia
Olivia Park
Infrastructure Lead
Quantify AI
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@quantify.ai>, Liam Chen <liam@quantify.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + SLO targets (Quantify / Redwood)

Thanks — Olivia, Liam. Confirming schedule for Thu 2027-07-29. Operational notes and immediate asks below.

Run schedule (PDT):
- 09:00 — kickoff, access & keys verified (Diego, Marissa on-call)
- 09:30–12:30 — Pass A (A100 baseline): synthetic + replay traffic
- 12:30–13:30 — lunch and quick analysis
- 13:30–16:30 — Pass B (H100 w/ nvlink): streaming-focused tests and inter-GPU scatter checks
- 16:30–17:00 — saturation/fallback exercise and quick wrap

Immediate asks for Quantify before Thu: 
- Sandbox API keys + a minimal ACL list (IP ranges) — provide by EOD Wed if possible.
- Representative spike traces (two 10–12 minute windows) — olive_spike_v1.tar suggested filename.
- Confirm whether 30-day retention is acceptable for raw test logs (we can redact later).

Preliminary sizing recommendation (draft, will be finalized post-run):
- Conservative: 8 x A100 (reserved) with a 25% burst bucket — good for stable throughput and predictable cost.
- Optimized: 5 x H100 (reserved) with nvlink and higher single-GPU throughput — lower p95 on streaming and smaller concurrency footprint.
- Fallback behavior: route to a 4-bit quantized variant in the fallback pool (functional equivalence tests required).

Note on deterministic behavior across quantizations: we will run token-level regression checks during the fallback exercise. We cannot guarantee bit-for-bit identical outputs after aggressive quantization, but we will validate functional parity for downstream tasks and provide quantitative divergence metrics.

On-call list for Thu (primary):
- Diego Fernandez (solutions) — diego_fernandez@redwood.com
- Marissa Cole (SRE) — marissa_cole@redwood.com
- Aditya Rao (ML infra) — aditya_rao@redwood.com
- Rafael Mendes (runtime) — rafael_mendes@redwood.com

I'll upload the runbook and the sizing matrix after Pass A completes; attaching the draft sizing matrix and a small artifact bundle for the Quantify team to review.

Looking forward to the run.

Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: quantify-demo-artifacts.zip, redwood-dedicated-sizing-matrix.xlsx
